page: Microsoft Azure M64bds_v3 is a memory-optimized virtual machine built on Microsoft Hyper-V virtualization. The instance provides 64 vCPUs derived from 32 physical cores across an Intel Xeon 8473C processor running at up to 4.0 GHz. Supporting the compute subsystem is 512.0 GB of system memory, maintaining an 8:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio with 8.0 GB per vCPU. Hardware capabilities include 105 MB of L3 cache alongside support for AVX-512, AMX Tile, and AMX INT8 vector and matrix extensions. For scratch storage and caching, the instance includes 429 GB of local SSD capacity, with no integrated GPU accelerators.

Benchmark measurements place the instance within the top 25% across several throughput metrics. Its uncached large-block memory read bandwidth reached 217.42 GB/sec, while write operations achieved 92.79 GB/sec. Compute evaluation yields a PassMark CPU score of 67019.35 and Geekbench multi-core score of 19901.0, paired with strong database operation scores of 29486.7. In-memory data throughput is highlighted by 71.51 million Redis SET operations per second and 74.63 GB/sec static web serving bandwidth. Small-scale CPU-based LLM prompt processing reached 2751.28 tokens/sec on a 135M model, though text generation on larger 70B models moderates to 4.01 tokens/sec.

Cost efficiency is focused around high-density memory provisioning rather than raw compute scale. The substantial RAM allocation and high memory read/write bandwidth make it effective for footprints demanding large data residency, reducing the need for horizontal multi-node partitioning. However, organizations with strictly compute-intensive or GPU-accelerated pipelines face resource overhead from unutilized memory capacity.

The hardware configuration suits large in-memory databases, enterprise relational database systems, extensive caching layers such as Redis clusters, and large data transformation pipelines. Its AMX support also enables CPU-based matrix operations and moderate-scale model inference where dedicated accelerators are not required.
